subtitle: Lesson 20 · Shor's Algorithm & Its Practical Limitations

steps.label: Given composite N = p × q, find p and q
steps.sub: Multiplying two large primes is cheap; reversing it is dramatically harder

steps.label: This asymmetry is a one-way function
steps.sub: Exactly what RSA exploits for its security guarantee

steps.label: RSA's public key includes N; the private key needs p and q
steps.sub: Factor N back → reconstruct the private key → break the encryption

steps.label: A claim about difficulty, not mathematical impossibility
steps.sub: Nobody has found a fast enough classical way — that's all that's known

code:
GNFS (best classical algorithm):
  exp(O(n^(1/3) * (log n)^(2/3)))   -- sub-exponential

Shor's algorithm:
  O(n^3) gate operations            -- polynomial
caption: Sub-exponential is slower than any polynomial but faster than brute force — exactly why doubling RSA's key size made factoring far harder, not just twice as hard.

steps.label: Grover's speedup: quadratic, same complexity class
steps.sub: Both classical and quantum stay exponential (or both polynomial) — just different exponents

steps.label: Shor's speedup: changes the complexity class itself
This is why factoring made cryptographers pay attention
steps.sub: Not a bigger number — a different kind of problem entirely
